samples.sample_label: 0.04Nb steel aged at 723 K for 6 h

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Ingot prepared by induction melting in a water-cooled copper crucible; re-melted and poured into a rotating copper mold at high speed to obtain steel strips of 60 × 70 × 2.5 mm under near-rapid solidification.
Extended aging treatment at 723 K for 6 h conducted on both the 0.02Nb and 0.04Nb steels to investigate the effect of aging period on microstructure and mechanical properties.

structures.overall_structure: Two-phase microstructure consisting of austenite (γ) matrix with irregular δ-ferrite; intragranular nano-scale κ-carbides and submicron NbC particles are present. After aging at 723 K for 6 h, the primary phases remain ferrite and austenite with no observable new diffraction peak.

phases_present.morphology: irregular-shaped ferrite randomly dispersed in the austenite matrix; phase boundaries irregular with numerous irregular bulges

precipitates.distribution: intragranular, dense and uniformly dispersed; volume fraction 18.7 vol%
submicron white particles within the austenite matrix; size significantly increases with prolongation of aging period

interfaces.phase_evolution: Prolonged 723 K aging promotes κ-carbide growth and coarsening; ferrite/austenite phase boundaries become irregular.
interfaces.interface_notes: No coarsened intergranular κ-carbides reported; only intragranular κ-carbides were characterized.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: gauge width 4 mm, gauge length 12 mm
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: minimum of four repetitions per steel strip

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: 723 K/6 h (red) curve of the 0.04Nb steel reaches the highest plateau (approaching 1200 MPa) but stops near 17% strain.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: yield strength and total elongation after 723 K/6 h

characterization_methods.purpose: Phase identification of 0.04Nb steel aged at 723 K for 3/6/9 h
characterization_methods.key_findings: Primary phases remain ferrite and austenite; no observable new diffraction peak in the 723 K/6 h aged 0.04Nb steel.

characterization_methods.purpose: Microstructure observation and ferrite content measurement
characterization_methods.key_findings: Irregular ferrite dispersed in austenite matrix; ferrite content 17.5 vol%; phase boundaries irregular with bulges; NbC particles coarsen with prolonged aging.
κ-carbide volume fraction 18.7 vol%, average size 7 nm; coherent with austenite ([100]γ // [100]κ).

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: ambient temperature; strain rate 2.5 × 10^-4 s^-1; gauge width 4 mm, gauge length 12 mm
characterization_methods.key_findings: Yield strength 1010 ± 4 MPa, tensile strength 1104 ± 5 MPa, total elongation 17 ± 1 %.

unmapped_findings: Measured chemical composition of the 0.04Nb steel strip (Table 1): Mn 12.82, Al 9.12, Cr 2.99, C 1.40, Nb 0.039, Fe Bal. (wt%).
For both the 0.02Nb and 0.04Nb steels, the aging treatment at 723 K for 6 h could result in good comprehensive mechanical properties.

Extended aging at 723 K does not markedly alter the yield strength of Nb-containing steels: κ-carbide precipitation strengthening intensifies while dislocation strengthening diminishes (grain boundary strengthening remains relatively unchanged).
Compared to 0.02Nb steels, the size of NbC particles in 0.04Nb steels significantly increases with the prolongation of aging period.
